newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar rebounds, but Euro-bourses stay mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar rebounds, but Euro-bourses stay mixed.

text.p: The dollar rebounded to its session highs on Wednesday as market sentiment switched, but European bourses were unable to get much of a boost from Wall Street's record-breaking performance overnight.
Both French and German shares fell, but London bucked the trend by nudging towards an intraday record.

On the bond markets, German government bonds were a touch lower after bond futures stormed to a series of new highs on Tuesday. In London, government gilts spiked lower at the start then recovered after stronger than expected retail sales figures for January.
The dollar's soggy start was blamed by traders on the German Bundesbank and Japan's trade surplus showing an underlying uptrend.
But a reinvigorated sterling and an apparently milder Bundesbank attitude towards the dollar helped the U.S. currency rebound.

The German central bank's February monthly report and remarks from its chief Hans Tietmeyer weighed on the dollar in early trade. But a later report quoting a Bundesbank council member as saying a dollar level between 1.70 and 1.75 marks would not risk importing inflation into Germany gave the dollar a leg-up.
Sterling clawed back some of Tuesday's sharp losses, gaining four pfennigs after receiving a boost from higher-than-expected retail sales. By 1300 GMT it was quoted at 2.7347 marks.
January retail sales rose by 0.6 percent month-on-month against forecasts for a 0.3 percent rise and scored a year-on year rise of 4.6 percent against forecasts for a 3.9 percent increase.

"There is fairly robust underlying growth in retail sales still. So the theory that things are beginning to slow down, which in our view has always been exaggerated, may not be right," said Robert Prior, economist at HSBC James Capel.
The Italian lira had a rocky ride once more, falling to a three-month low near 1,000 per mark in early trade before recovering to 994.35 by 1300 GMT, up on late Tuesday's 996.73.

It was helped by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's announcement of a mini-budget which he said would enable Italy to meet the criteria for monetary union (EMU). Fears Italy might miss the first wave of EMU have buffeted the lira in recent days.
In contrast to French and German share markets, London opened higher, getting a boost from Wall Street and led higher by gains in B.A.T Industries and drug stocks.

The blue chip FTSE 100 index was trading just short record levels set earlier this month by mid-session, up 13.2 points at 4,345.5. But traders said gains were restrained by gilts and caution ahead of U.S. consumer price figures due later.
"We are toying with all-time highs and we could be squeezed a bit higher short-term with the cash that's out there," said the head of equity trading at one leading brokerage.

Bank stocks were in focus again after Tuesday's tumble in Barclays shares, after results at the low end of expectations. Barclays was down another 21 pence at 11.10-1/2 by 1300 GMT after dropping 70-1/2p on Tuesday.
B.A.T Industries was up 25p at 553 after a surge in U.S. tobacco stocks amid renewed hopes that the industry is taking steps to settle its litigation problems, though B.A.T played down the reports.
German shares ended bourse trade sharply lower, tracking Tuesday's post-bourse slide in electronic trade.
Traders said the market remained stable, however, with no serious correction not yet in sight.
The 30-share DAX-30 index ended at 3,233.75 points, down 42.41.
French shares started slightly higher, then turned lower, puzzling dealers after Wall Street's advance.
"It may be an erratic movement or start of consolidation. Pressure on the dollar may be worrying some. But the (French) market could go into reverse again," one trader said.
Thomson CSF rose 4.27 percent to 183 francs after the government announced the defence electronics firm would be sold by private sale.
CURRENCIES AT 1300 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6923 marks and 123.89 yen compared with 1.6904 marks and 123.94 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1300 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.2 points, or 0.3 percent, at 4,345.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 7.0 points, or 0.27 percent, at 2,610.52.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 42.41 points, or 1.29 percent, at 3,233.75
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $343.00 vs $337.70 previously. Silver was down three cents at $5.21.
